concepts.definition: The process by which people try to get others to confirm their existing self-concept.
The set of beliefs a person holds about their own traits, abilities and roles.
Acting in ways that draw responses that confirm one's self-view.
The wish for favorable evaluation of the self.

questions.q: What is the motive behind self-verification?
questions.a: A need for coherence and predictability: others should see the person as the person sees themselves.

questions.q: What did Kwang and Swann (2010) conclude about self-enhancement and self-verification?
questions.a: Both motives are influential and control different kinds of responses.

questions.q: Sam believes they are not leadership material and defers after a promotion. Which mechanism is this?
questions.a: Behavioral confirmation, which draws responses that confirm the self-view.
